episodes.191630: A backdoor front behind an upper level disturbance over the upper Midwest moved into far northeast NM the morning of July 7th. Additionally, a remnant outflow boundary was draped across far east central NM and west Texas. These two surface features combined with higher moisture resulted in the development of strong to severe storms across these areas during the mid afternoon and evening hours. Another round of storms moved across northeast and east central NM overnight as the backdoor front surged west through the gaps of the central mountain chain. Storms caused some isolated flooding across Cannon Air Force Base. Showers and storms exited into the Texas Panhandle during the mid morning hours on July 8th. Another round of strong to severe storms developed over the north central mountains midday July 8th with penny to nickel size hail observed in the Jemez Mountains and quarter size hail near Ute Park. Some flash flooding was also observed in Las Vegas. Storms dissipated over central New Mexico shortly after sunset.
episodes.191646: A few severe thunderstorms track southeast across the northeast Colorado plains dropping hail up to golf ball (1.75 inch) sized.
episodes.191724: Back-building thunderstorms trained over a small area led to localized flooding in Florence County, SC.
episodes.191736: A weak front acted as a trigger for multiple slow-moving thunderstorms with heavy rain that caused flash flooding in portions of east central GA.
episodes.192133: An approaching short wave trough interacted with a surface pressure trough, a stalled out cold front, strong heating, and abundant moisture to create prolific severe thunderstorm winds across portions of the South Plains and Rolling Plains on the afternoon of the seventh. By late in the afternoon, temperatures had warmed into the upper 90s to lower 100s across the central and western South Plains. At the same time, a surface low formed in the extreme southwestern Texas Panhandle with a surface pressure trough extending southward and a stalled out cold front extending eastward. The strong heating east and south of these features created a very unstable atmosphere able to develop thunderstorms. A multi-cell cluster of thunderstorms formed along these features and moved to the east during the late afternoon. A dry sub-cloud layer allowed these storms to produce numerous swaths of severe wind gusts, especially as they moved across Lubbock County. The storms eventually grew upscale into the Rolling Plains and weakened early in the evening. Additionally, a strong outflow boundary well out ahead of thunderstorms produced a severe wind gust of 61 mph at Plains (Yoakum County) measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.
episodes.192446: A cold front extending from Minnesota to Kansas triggered a broken line of thunderstorms west of the Mississippi River during the afternoon of July 7th.  As the line moved eastward, one of the cells within the line produced gusty winds of around 60 mph and minor wind damage near Rushville in Schuyler County.
episodes.193148: Thunderstorms that developed over western Kansas during the afternoon of the 6th, moved southeast and became more organized over western and central Oklahoma on the 7th. This band of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through eastern Oklahoma, producing isolated damaging wind gusts.
episodes.193384: A cold front and surface trough west of North Carolina approached in the afternoon and evening hours. Ahead of the boundary, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the southern Piedmont and tracked east-northeast into the central to eastern Piedmont and Coastal Plain of central North Carolina by the late afternoon and evening hours. Several reports of downed trees and power lines were reported in Wake, Harnett, and Johnston Counties, as well as some isolated flash flooding.
episodes.193511: The outer bands of Tropical Storm Beryl began to spread northwest across portions of West Central Louisiana and Deep East Texas during the early and mid afternoon hours of July 7th, as the parent tropical storm began to shift north across the Western Gulf of Mexico. Strong heating and instability were present ahead of this cyclone, with increasing large scale ascent contributing to the development of isolated severe thunderstorms as they intensified over Central Angelina County Texas. As a result, damaging winds downed several trees near and north of Lufkin before weakening.
episodes.193688: Thunderstorms, along an approaching cold front, initiated during the mid morning hours of July 6th in northwestern Lincoln County. This activity grew upscale and became severe during the late morning hours. As activity transitioned east, severe storms continued into the afternoon hours over portions of central and southwestern Nebraska. Hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter and thunderstorm wind gusts up to 60 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.193758: A high-amplitude (yet overall weak in magnitude) upper trough rotated across the central CONUS on the 7th. Scattered thunderstorms developed along a quasi-stationary boundary across portions of western and central Oklahoma during the early evening of the 7th. Strong instability and sufficient deep-layer wind shear emerged along and south of the aforementioned boundary, fostering a mix of multi-cell and transiently organized (supercell) storm modes. Damaging wind gusts and large hail occurred with a few thunderstorms across south-central into southern Oklahoma.
episodes.193932: During the late afternoon and early evening hours of the 6th a couple of supercells formed over the south-central Texas Panhandle. These thunderstorms generally moved from northwest to southeast and ended up producing winds up to 59 mph and hail up to the size of ping pong balls in parts of Carson and Armstrong County.
episodes.194060: Increasing warm and moist air into Iowa, along with a shortwave arriving into the afternoon to evening and developing LLJ led to the development of areas of showers and thunderstorms. Favorable shear and instability parameters overhead led to at least a few severe thunderstorms, generally occurring over northern into parts of central Iowa. In particular, Humboldt county down to Story county experienced severe hail ranging between 1-1.5 inches, largest in the town of Bode, as well as thunderstorm wind damage.
episodes.194077: Isolated thunderstorms along a warm front moved across southeast WI. Some minor tree damage occurred.
episodes.194088: Following showers and thunderstorms over Iowa during the morning hours with a passing shortwave, an additional shortwave arriving in the Central Plains with the aid of increased lift and MUCAPE values around 1000 J/kg overhead brought another round of scattered showers and storms into the afternoon and evening hours. These multiple rounds of convection, along with the slow-moving nature of some storms led to heavy rainfall and eventually flash flooding, particularly over Wright county. Reports of flooded roads and rainfall totals averaging between 3-5 inches were common. Severe wind was also reported in Adair county.
episodes.194138: A weak trough and area of low pressure moved into the Northland during the afternoon hours on the 26th. A few thunderstorms developed across the region by late afternoon and brought some small hail to the Duluth area. Later in the evening, a collapsing storm brought some localized wind damage to a property near Malmo.
episodes.194142: Low pressure located over northern Minnesota the afternoon of July 7th led to the development of scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms over northeastern Minnesota and northwestern Wisconsin. Most of this activity was very shallow in nature and were not producing hail larger than peas or much in terms of wind gusts. One shower produced a waterspout over Lake Vermilion shortly before 2:30 PM CDT. Waterspouts and funnel clouds were possible across the region due to favorable atmospheric conditions in the vicinity of the low pressure center over the region. This survey was conducted utilizing photos and videos of the waterspout that were posted to social media and through interviews with witnesses. No injuries or fatalities were reported and the waterspout likely remained over open waters of Lake Vermilion.
episodes.194171: During the late afternoon hours, a line of thunderstorms developed over East-Central Colorado and moved southeast into Kit Carson County. The tail end storm of the line produced a swath of accumulating hail up to golf ball in size from the northwest side of Seibert to southwest of Stratton. The largest hail fell in Seibert and southwest of Stratton. There was some hail damage to a vehicle traveling on I-70.
episodes.194181: During the evening hours on July 7th a slow moving thunderstorm moved over portions of northwestern Clark County. These storms produced heavy rainfall totals which resulted in some flooding along County Road O near Greenwood. Additionally, other storms produced small hail in Taylor County.
episodes.194214: Marginal mixed-layer instability and effective bulk shear around 30 knots led to weak organization of scattered storms during the late afternoon and evening hours from eastern South Dakota into southwest Minnesota. The strongest cells produced up to quarter size hail. A deeper sub-cloud dry layer supported spotty stronger wind gusts.
episodes.194215: A couple of short-lived stronger storms with hail up to half-dollar size developed along a weak boundary moving into an airmass with around 1000 J/kg MLCAPE and fairly weak shear.
episodes.194255: A shortwave moved across central Wyoming and tapped into mid level moisture to produce scattered showers and thunderstorms. Dry low levels led to the storms being high based and several locations experienced strong wind gusts from microbursts. The airports near Greybull, Casper and Buffalo reported wind gusts of 58 mph or greater.
episodes.194261: Hurricane Beryl moved into Texas during the morning of July 8th. Gusty winds, scattered flooding, and an isolated tornado occurred in deep southeast Texas as the system moved through the region.
episodes.194497: Beginning around 7 pm, severe Thunderstorms spread into the area with a mix of impacts ranging from quarter to ping pong ball sized hail and severe wind gusts, reported as high as 70 mph, as was reported by the Garden City Airport observation at 9:20 pm. A torrential rain environment was also in place, as street flooding quickly developed in the town of Scott City. The severe weather continued into the overnight and early morning hours of July 7tt,  as 67 mph winds were measured by the mesonet station near Copeland around 2 AM. A prolific outflow boundary developed, moving across Gray county. A Damage survey conducted yielded estimated 100 mph wind gusts 5 miles southwest of Charleston.
episodes.194639: A deep low pressure system loitered over the Northern Plains and Upper Midwest for multiple days, producing many funnel clouds over western and central North Dakota over a four day period. One funnel touched down, becoming a tornado, in Mountrail County. The touchdown occurred on a farmstead where multiple campers were parked. One camper was rolled, causing significant damage. In addition, a small grain bin had its roof torn off. The tornado then proceeded into an open field before dissipating. Based on the damage done the tornado was rated EF-1, with winds estimated at 90 MPH.
episodes.194648: A slow moving to near stationary frontal boundary initiated afternoon thunderstorms along the I20 and I85 corridor. Ample instability and moisture allowed a couple storms to become strong and water-logged. Gusty winds from microbursts caused wind damage from Chamblee down through Panthersville. Slow moving thunderstorms instigated flash flooding in the eastern Atlanta metro.
episodes.194669: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.194828: Thunderstorms in Lee County produced damaging winds during the afternoon hours.
episodes.194881: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the North Carolina Piedmont during the afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief severe weather in the form of damaging wind gusts.
episodes.194946: Rain that fell during the month of June across Minnesota and Wisconsin caused rises on the Mississippi River, along the Iowa and Illinois border. Additionally, heavy rain that fell locally in July helped to prolong the crest and delay the river falling below flood stage, especially south of the Wapsipinicon, Rock, and Iowa Rivers.
episodes.195034: SPI Brazos Santiago reported a peak wind gust of 39 kts or 45 mph, possibly as a result of a nearby outflow boundary. The outflow emanated from distant bands loosely associated with Tropical Storm Beryl, whose center was more than 130 miles east-southeast of this location when the event occurred.
episodes.195186: On the 6th and the 7th of the month, a longwave trough was centered over the central CONUS. At the surface, several wandering surface boundaries initiated isolated convection the afternoons and evenings of the 6th, 7th and 8th. A few of these storms produced funnel clouds which never touched the ground, though they garnered a lot of social media attention. Isolated instances of strong winds and severe hail were also noted across parts of eastern Nebraska and southwest Iowa.
episodes.195187: On the 6th and the 7th of the month, a longwave trough was centered over the central CONUS. At the surface, several wandering surface boundaries initiated isolated convection the afternoons and evenings of the 6th, 7th and 8th. A few of these storms produced funnel clouds which never touched the ground, though they garnered a lot of social media attention. Isolated instances of strong winds and severe hail were also noted across parts of eastern Nebraska and southwest Iowa.

The waterspout developed to the northwest of Echo Point and west of Ely Island on eastern Lake Vermilion. Based on radar and video of the waterspout, it moved slowly to the north-northeast before dissipating near Spider Island. It may have passed near or over Spider Island. It also passed through the vicinity of Taylor and Stonich islands. As of this time, no damage reports have been received from these islands which do have structures on them, so the waterspout may have remained over the water. Based on photos and videos, the waterspout was about 30 yards wide and was on the water for about 2 miles. No fatalities or injuries have been reported.
